title: Ride-hailing app (Uber / Lyft style) client
summary: Real-time driver tracking on a map, a robust trip state machine that survives app termination, and location updates that balance accuracy with battery.
requirements: Rider: set pickup/dropoff, see nearby cars, request, track driver in real time, pay, rate.
Driver: go online, stream location every few seconds, accept trips, navigate.
Trip state must be correct after app restarts or network loss.
components: Location service (CLLocationManager / `CLLocationUpdate.liveUpdates`) with accuracy tuned per state
Real-time channel (WebSocket) for driver positions and trip events; push for background state changes
Trip state machine on the server; client mirrors it and re-syncs on launch
Map layer with smooth marker interpolation between updates
Live Activity for trip status on Lock Screen and Dynamic Island
tradeoffs: Frequent high-accuracy GPS gives smooth tracking but drains battery; reduce frequency when idle and use significant-change monitoring.
Client-side interpolation smooths movement but can show slightly wrong positions.
Server-authoritative state is consistent; client predictions make UI feel faster but must reconcile.
body: **Trip states:** requesting → matched → driverArriving → onTrip → completed / cancelled. Every transition comes from the server with a version; the client renders the latest version and ignores older events.

**Driver location stream:** driver app sends location every 4s while online (batched if offline); server indexes by geohash/H3 cell for nearby searches; rider subscribes to their driver's channel only.
**Smooth marker:** animate between consecutive points over the update interval; snap to road if available; rotate by bearing.
**Background:** drivers need the location background mode and 'Always' permission with clear justification; riders do not.
**Failure modes:** socket drops (fall back to polling every 5s), GPS drift in tunnels, duplicate requests (idempotency key on 'request ride'), payment failure after trip.
